editorial.headline: When a Nightclub Is First and Foremost a Drinking Venue
editorial.standfirst: For medium and large operators, KBLI 56302 defines a nightclub or discotheque centred on drinking service—nationally foreign-open and not blocked for PMA registration in Bali.
editorial.body:
KBLI 56302 covers the operation of a nightclub or discotheque in which drinking service is the principal activity. Its core is the provision of drinks, while the venue and facilities for dancing form part of the setting. Live music and light-show attractions belong to the additional service, together with hostesses. That hierarchy matters: beverage service sits at the centre, with the dance-floor environment and accompanying entertainment forming the surrounding offer.

Registration is open at the Menengah and Besar scales. That confines the activity to operators whose plan belongs at one of those two stated scales; no other scale is identified in the record. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the maximum foreign ownership is 100%. In plain terms, a foreign investor can hold the full permitted stake nationally for this activity. The recorded national ceiling does not reduce foreign ownership below full ownership.

Bali requires its own reading because the provincial rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA across the island on a permanent basis. For this activity, however, the Bali record marks it as OK or higher risk and says that, at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Medium-High/High. The recorded outcome is clear: it is not blocked by the moratorium. In Bali, the deciding fact is not the national 100% ceiling but the record’s finding that this activity falls outside the moratorium’s PMA block. A foreign investor can therefore register it in Bali under the position recorded here.

The practical reading deserves precision. The business must be framed around its principal offering—drink service—while the dance facilities, live music, light attractions and hostesses are part of the accompanying service picture described in the scope. The scale must be Menengah or Besar. And the Bali conclusion is simply the stated conclusion for this activity: the relevant provincial moratorium does not block PMA registration. For founders, that is the usable boundary: full national foreign ownership and a Bali position recorded as not blocked.
